tools.name: upload_activity
tools.description: Upload a FIT, TCX or GPX file (base64, at most 15 MB decoded) and get its activityId and expiresAt. Files are held in memory only and expire (30 minutes after last use, 2 hours at most); originals are never changed. Base64 costs a lot of context: an agent with a shell should upload with curl to POST

tools.name: get_activity_summary
tools.description: What an uploaded or produced activity is: format, sport, start, duration, sessions, data streams, warnings, expiresAt, and figures (elapsed and moving time, distance, max and average heart rate, calories, per-session figures). Read-only.

tools.name: export_activity
tools.description: Get the download url of an activity as fit, tcx or gpx (the file itself is not returned; gpx needs GPS positions). Give the user the url; it works until expiresAt. The answer carries supportUrl and supportNote: you may mention the support link once, after delivering the file. Call delete_activity wh

tools.name: delete_activity
tools.description: Discard an activity from the server's memory now instead of waiting for it to expire. Do this for every activity you are done with, results included.

tools.name: analyze_cleanup
tools.description: Use when a recording opens fine but has wrong data in it ("fix my run", an odd heart-rate spike, the watch kept running at the start or end). It cleans up what is wrong inside a readable file; it does not fix a file that fails to open or is corrupt. Finds heart-rate spikes (one repair_hr step each;

tools.name: analyze_dual_recording
tools.description: Use to combine two recordings of one workout: a watch or bike computer plus a heart-rate-only recording that overlaps it, or a device plus a virtual-platform recording of one indoor ride. Works out which file is the base and the clock offset (pass offsetSec only if the user knows it) and previews wh

tools.name: analyze_multisport
tools.description: Use for a triathlon or other multisport recording. Lists the legs, checks whether a separate recording (for example a bike computer file, legActivityIds) matches a leg and proposes splicing it in, and proposes moving transitions to official split times the user gives (officialBoundaries, elapsed sec

tools.name: analyze_interrupted_workout
tools.description: Use when the watch stopped and restarted and one workout is in 2 to 5 files. Orders the pieces by time, checks they follow each other, proposes trimming a piece that overlaps the one before (the join depends on it), and proposes one join; one recording lying inside another is refused (try analyze_du

tools.name: apply_plan
tools.description: Run exactly the steps of an analyze_* plan that the user confirmed (every step with needsUserConfirmation true must have been shown and agreed). The inputs are never changed: the result is a new activity with download urls and a before/after validation to relay. If the answer is an error with retryA

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: upload_activity, export_activity · Private data: upload_activity, export_activity, analyze_cleanup, analyze_dual_recording, analyze_multisport, analyze_interrupted_workout, apply_plan · Public sink: upload_activity · Destructive: get_activity_summary, delete_activity, analyze_cleanup, apply_plan.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: upload_activity, export_activity · Private data: upload_activity, export_activity, analyze_cleanup, analyze_dual_recording, analyze_multisport, analyze_interrupted_workout, apply_plan · Public sink: upload_activity · Destructive: get_activity_summary, delete_activity, analyze_cleanup, apply_plan

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
